rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act – Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources
rules.requirement: If your landlord plans to end your tenancy, they must give you a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time as the notice to quit or non-renewal, and must file a copy of that notice with the City. If you don't get it, report it to the Office of Fair Housing and Equity (617-635-2500 or 311). The violation does not stop the eviction.
rules.key_value: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources delivered with notice to quit/non-renewal

coverage.summary: All landlords, and foreclosing owners for the City filing, in Boston who plan to end a tenancy agreement.

rules.penalty: Enforced by Inspectional Services Department: warning for the 1st offense; $300 per day for the 2nd and later offenses. Failure to submit the notice to the City's portal may result in a fine of up to $300 per day. A violation does not halt the eviction process.
rules.citation: Boston City Ordinances § 10-11.7 (Housing Stability Notification Act)
rules.quoted_span: The Housing Stability Notification Act requires any landlord to provide renters with a Notice of Tenant’s Rights and Resources when planning to end a tenancy agreement.

notes: The HSNA is a notice and reporting requirement for ending a tenancy. It does not require just cause to evict. It is classified under just_cause_eviction only because it is an eviction-notice rule, so review the category fit. The page states no effective date. The citation section number comes from the page's penalty table.
